subject: IP assignment and training carveouts - order form redlines
messages:
From: Courtney Li <courtney.li@skyline.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline Legal <legal@skyline.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify IP assignment in MSA/order form

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team liked the latency and the routing options. Legal and procurement reviewed the draft MSA/order form and have questions about the IP sections before we can move to procurement. High-level asks: 

- Skyline needs clear assignment rights for "Customer Outputs" created by our users (we'd prefer assignment for productization). Can you confirm Redwood's position on output assignment vs license?
- Training/data use: our security team wants an opt-in model for allowing customer outputs or telemetry to be used for model training (we cannot allow blanket training rights).
- Feedback license: can Redwood retain a limited feedback license for product quality and debugging only, with anonymization guarantees?

Attached is a short list of questions and an initial annotated redline (Skyline_MSA_questions.docx). Procurement timeline is tight — aiming to finalize redlines by next week.

Could you loop in whoever owns licensing?

Thanks,
Courtney
Courtney Li
Head of Product, Skyline Analytics
courtney.li@skyline.com

Attachment: Skyline_MSA_questions.docx (list of numbered questions)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Courtney Li <courtney.li@skyline.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify IP assignment in MSA/order form

Hi Courtney — thanks for the clear notes and the timeline. Looping in Jordan (sales lead) and Laura (contracts counsel) to coordinate a tidy response. Quick position from product/sales perspective: 

- Output ownership: Redwood does not typically assign the underlying model or model weights. For customer outputs we can offer either (a) an exclusive/perpetual assignment of specific outputs limited to the customer’s product, or (b) a broad, perpetual, non-exclusive assignment for outputs depending on the term and commercial tier. We need to pick the right commercial trigger.
- Training rights: we can offer an opt-in "training license" that is limited, timeboxed, and only applies to anonymized telemetry unless the customer explicitly agrees to stronger use.
- Feedback: we can accept a limited license for debugging and quality improvements, with commitments to remove any PII and to aggregate telemetry.

I'll attach a proposed Order Form excerpt that highlights suggested language for each option. Laura — could you please propose contract language and advise on fallback we can offer if Skyline insists on assignment-of-outputs for productization?

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment: Proposed_OrderForm_v2.pdf (marked-up excerpt)

Team — quick internal plan to respond to Skyline: 

1) Commercial options to offer (pick one based on deal tier):
   - Option A (Standard): Customer receives a perpetual, non-exclusive license to Customer Outputs with rights to reproduce and distribute; Redwood retains all underlying model IP.
   - Option B (Premium): Limited assignment of generated Outputs for specific product lines (customer holds assignment for those outputs only); requires higher commitment (annual minimum).
2) Training carveout: provide an explicit opt-in checkbox and a short data-retention/PII-exclusion addendum.
3) Feedback/telemetry: accept limited, anonymized feedback license; no re-training on raw customer content without opt-in.

Laura/Ben — can legal produce redlines for Option B fallback language that preserves Redwood's right to maintain and improve the runtime (we cannot accept assignment for underlying model or internal datasets)? We should include a one-sentence escrow/rollback safety for extreme dispute scenarios.

If procurement needs final wording by next Tue, let's aim to send Skyline a formal offer today with both Option A and Option B language so they can pick. Asking Neha to confirm and send.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Skyline Legal <legal@skyline.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Skyline redlines (annotated)

Neha/Jordan — attaching our annotated redline. Key points from our side: 

- Skyline requires assignment of Customer Outputs (we want to be able to ship features built from generated outputs without ongoing license fees).
- Training: we cannot accept any language that permits Redwood to train on outputs derived from our confidential user data without explicit, document-level opt-in.
- Telemetry: allowable for debugging only if fully anonymized and not used to re-train models for revenue-generating features without opt-in.

Procurement is asking for a committed bundle for signature by EOD Friday — if Redwood can provide a clear commercial option that includes output assignment for productization we can sign quickly. Otherwise we may need to escalate.

Regards,
Skyline Legal (on behalf of Courtney Li)
legal@skyline.com

Attachment: Skyline_Redlines_20250709.docx (annotated MSA/Order Form)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Courtney Li <courtney.li@skyline.com>, legal@skyline.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify IP assignment in MSA/order form — Redwood response and path forward

Courtney / Skyline Legal — thanks for the redlines and the timeline. Below is Redwood's formal response and the offer we can put on the table today. We kept the language short to reduce contract back-and-forth: 

Summary offer (pick A or B):

Option A (no assignment; broad customer rights):
- Customer receives a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive right to use, reproduce, and distribute Customer Outputs for its internal and commercial purposes.
- Redwood retains all rights in the underlying model, code, and training data.
- Training: Redwood will not use Customer Outputs or Customer Content for model training unless Skyline opts in via a separate written addendum.
- Feedback/telemetry: Redwood may use anonymized, aggregated telemetry for product quality and debugging; no product-feature re-training on raw customer content without opt-in.

Option B (assignment for productization — limited):
- For customers who commit to the Premium bundle (minimum annual commitment: $X), Redwood will assign title to Customer Outputs produced under the Agreement for specific product SKUs defined in the Order Form.
- Assignment is limited to the Customer Outputs themselves and does not include any assignment of Redwood's models, weights, or proprietary artifacts.
- Training: same opt-in approach as Option A.
- Telemetry/feedback: same anonymization guarantees and limited license for debug/quality.

Contract mechanics and fallbacks:
- We will include explicit PII exclusion language and a short data-protection addendum.
- If Skyline requires assignment for all outputs across all product lines (no SKU limit), Redwood needs C-level approval; this is out-of-the-box for our standard MSA. We can escalate but would need commercial uplift.
- Proposed next step: Redwood sends a single tracked redline that implements Option A and Option B as selectable clauses in the Order Form. Skyline confirms selection and procurement issues PO/DocuSign link.

I've attached a short offer doc we can push to procurement now. Laura/Ben — please review the Option B assignment wording in the attached doc and flag anything that would create operational risk (escrow, rollback, model maintenance). Jordan — please confirm the commercial uplift and I'll send to Courtney.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: Skyline_Response_Offer_20250710.docx (Option A/B language), Proposed_OrderForm_v2.pdf
